en.intro: Arjuna has just seen the universal form and now confesses all his casual slights. Listen to how he names his own carelessness.
en.notice: Listen to the word ekah, alone. Arjuna asks for forgiveness for both private errors and public ones, showing he holds nothing back before the divine form.
en.next: Arjuna now calls Krishna the supreme object of reverence, the greatest teacher, and the father of all beings.
en.meaning: Whatever disrespect I showed you in jest, while walking, resting, sitting, eating, alone or before others, I ask your immeasurable forgiveness.

hi.intro: अर्जुन ने अभी-अभी विश्वरूप देखा है और अब वह अपनी सारी लापरवाही स्वीकार करता है। सुनिए, वह अपनी भूलों को कैसे स्वीकार करता है।
hi.meaning: हे अच्युत, चलते-फिरते, सोते-जागते, उठते-बैठते और अकेले अथवा दूसरों के सामने हँसी-मज़ाक में मैंने आपका जो भी तिरस्कार किया है, उसके लिए मैं आपसे क्षमा माँगता हूँ।
hi.notice: एक शब्द सुनिए, एकः, यानी अकेले। अर्जुन अकेले या दूसरों के सामने की गई हर गलती के लिए माफ़ी माँगता है, जिससे पता चलता है कि वह ईश्वर के सामने कुछ भी छिपा नहीं रहा है।
hi.next: इसके बाद वे कहते हैं कि आप सभी प्राणियों के पिता, परम पूज्य और परम गुरु हैं।

en.intro: Arjuna has just seen the universal form and now confesses all his casual slights. Listen to how he names his own carelessness.
en.body: Whatever disrespect I showed you in jest, while walking, resting, sitting, eating, alone or before others, I ask your immeasurable forgiveness. Listen to the word ekah, alone. Arjuna asks for forgiveness for both private errors and public ones, showing he holds nothing back before the divine form. Arjuna now calls Krishna the supreme object of reverence, the greatest teacher, and the father of all beings.

issues: wrong_fact: "next: He then declares Krishna the father and supreme teacher of all existence." (The English 'next' misdescribes the next verse. The next verse (43) declares Krishna as the father of all beings, the supreme object of reverence, and the greatest teacher, not just 'the father and supreme teacher'. More importantly, the Hindi 'next' presents the content of the NEXT verse (verse 43) as if it is part of the current verse's meaning (42).)
